exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS, attackers can intercept and impersonate either party in a connection, enabling adversary-in-the-middle attacks.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of mutual TLS allows attackers to use forged or self-signed certificates to impersonate services since client certificates are not validated.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol or Service Impersonation
exploitedBy.relevance: Without mutual TLS enforcement, malicious services can impersonate legitimate ones as there is no cryptographic proof of identity on both sides.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Root Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Bypassing certificate validation can be achieved by installing rogue root certificates, undermining the chain of trust.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Certificate validation bypass allows forged or stolen certificates to be accepted, enabling unauthorized authentication.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Install Digital Certificate
exploitedBy.relevance: Attackers can install malicious digital certificates to exploit systems that skip proper certificate validation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Downgrade Attack
exploitedBy.relevance: TLS protocol downgrade directly maps to this technique where attackers force use of weaker protocol versions to enable decryption or exploitation.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Weaken Encryption
exploitedBy.relevance: Downgrading TLS effectively weakens the encryption strength, allowing adversaries to intercept or decrypt traffic.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Replay attacks on service requests often involve reusing captured tokens or credentials to gain unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal Application Access Token
exploitedBy.relevance: Captured tokens from service requests can be replayed by attackers to impersonate legitimate service calls.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Service Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted service discovery traffic exposes service topology and endpoints, aiding adversary network reconnaissance.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Cloud Service Discovery
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted cloud service discovery traffic allows attackers to enumerate available cloud services and their configurations.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: DNS
exploitedBy.relevance: Unencrypted DNS-based service discovery reveals infrastructure details that adversaries can exploit for targeting.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Service Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Without rate limiting, attackers can flood individual services to exhaust resources and cause denial of service.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Application Exhaustion Flood
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of per-service rate limiting enables application-layer exhaustion attacks targeting specific microservices.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Private Keys
exploitedBy.relevance: Gaps in certificate rotation extend the window during which compromised private keys can be exploited by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Digital Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Certificate rotation gaps allow adversaries more time to discover and exploit certificate information gathered through reconnaissance.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Network Boundary Bridging
exploitedBy.relevance: Lack of east-west segmentation allows attackers to bridge network boundaries and move laterally between services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Exploitation of Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Without east-west segmentation, a compromised service can directly exploit remote services across the environment.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: External Remote Services
exploitedBy.relevance: Unsegmented east-west traffic enables lateral movement by treating internal services as accessible remote services.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Encrypted Channel
exploitedBy.relevance: TLS termination at a shared proxy creates a segment of unencrypted traffic, undermining end-to-end encrypted channel guarantees.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Asymmetric Cryptography
exploitedBy.relevance: Shared proxy TLS termination exposes the asymmetric cryptography keys at a shared trust boundary, increasing risk of key compromise.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Protocol Tunneling
exploitedBy.relevance: A compromised shared proxy can be abused for protocol tunneling to exfiltrate data decrypted during TLS termination.
